general: The horns of Rohan split the dawn and ten thousand horsemen poured over the ridge like a golden wave breaking on black iron.
Shields were shattered and spears were broken and still the line held, because the men of Gondor did not know how to do otherwise.
The oliphaunts came from the south in a line, each one a moving fortress, and the ground shook under them like a drumbeat.
Fell deeds awoke; fire and slaughter; spear was shaken, shield was splintered, and the age of the sword had returned.
Not one of them expected to see another sunrise, and that knowledge burned away everything except the simple duty of the next sword stroke.
The dead had come and behind them came their king, and the Enemy's armies broke against that ghost-tide like water against stone.
In the din of battle, thought ceases; there is only the body, the weapon, and the opponent, and the terrible clarity of pure survival.
The Battle of Pelennor Fields was the largest convergence of armies since the Last Alliance, and the cost of it would be counted for generations.
Charge! Charge! Forth Eorlingas! The hills shook with the sound of it and the enemy ranks wavered in the face of that magnificent and terrible fury.
When the last orc fell and the last horn fell silent, those who had survived looked at one another without knowing what expression to make.
There is a cost to every victory that the songs never quite capture — the weight of the living who must bury the dead.
The Eagles are coming! The Eagles are coming! And in that moment the impossible became merely improbable, which was enough.
Grond, the wolf-head battering ram, hammered at the gate three times, and at the third blow the gate fell and the city held its breath.
aragorn: Hold your ground! Sons of Gondor, of Rohan, my brothers — I see in your eyes the same fear that would take the heart of me.
A day may come when the courage of men fails, when we forsake our friends and break all bonds of fellowship — but it is not this day.
This day we fight! By all that you hold dear on this good earth, I bid you stand, men of the West!
The sword of Elendil is reforged and I carry it into battle; let those who serve the dark see what it means to stand against the returning king.
We go to certain death, some of us — and that has never yet stopped a man of Gondor from going.
gandalf: The battle belongs to those who ride; I shall hold the rear and keep what light I can in this darkening hour.
Shadowfax, show us the meaning of haste! There is yet time to turn this tide if we arrive before the gate falls.
I am a servant of the Secret Fire and I will not yield this bridge to anything that walks, crawls, or flies in the dark.
The battle of Helm's Deep is over; the battle for Middle-earth is about to begin, and I think we should try to win both.
legolas: They're taking the hobbits to Isengard! — and I can see it from here, which is considerably further away than any of you can see.
A cave troll — my arrow count is now at seventeen, and I intend to improve that number considerably before this battle is done.
That still only counts as one! I don't care how large the beast was; the rules of the count do not change for dramatic effect.
gimli: Certainty of death, small chance of success — what are we waiting for? Let us go and at least make it a story worth telling.
I never thought I'd die fighting alongside an elf, and yet here we are; shall we agree that whoever saves the other buys the drinks after?
sauron: My armies are numberless and my patience is eternal; you fight battles that delay the inevitable by hours and buy yourselves only pain.
Send them my regards — the Witch-king, the Balrog, the dragon-fire and the battering-ram; let them know I do not share my power with the victorious.
Every soldier who falls defending your walls is one less argument for hope; I am counting on that arithmetic.
